ready1_open_rewrite.raw_question_text: The output voltage of a boost converter circuit is a function of the input voltage and the duty cycle of the switching signal, represented by the variable D (ranging in value from 0% to 100%), where \( D = \frac{t_{on}}{t_{on} + t_{off}} \). Based on this mathematical relationship, calculate the output voltage of this converter circuit at a duty cycle D=0% , assuming an input voltage of 40 volts. The output voltage is ______V.

ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: Image description: The attached figure shows a boost converter circuit labeled “Boost converter circuit”; the left input terminal is labeled Vin, there is a switch in the middle with duty cycle labeled D, the right output terminal is labeled Vout, and the relationship formula Vout = Vin / (1 - D) is given in the figure. Reasoning calculation: The problem gives the input voltage Vin = 40 V and the duty cycle D = 0%. Convert 0% to a decimal as D = 0. Substitute into the formula in the figure: Vout = 40 / (1 - 0) = 40 / 1 = 40 V.
